title: a-superseded-decision-is-retired-through-the-rehearsal-door
intention: A superseded decision line on a ticket is retired through the rehearsal door, so the reader stops being handed two contradicting instructions while the file keeps the old text and who retired it.
why: Measured 2026-10-06 on 45c168cc1ff1: `cairn rehearse --decide` only appends (rehearsal.py decide()), so D22, D31 and D32 each corrected D3 while D3's wrong text ('bin/cairn test --seal on the loop proof') stayed on the ticket. Round 9 returned 'cannot_proceed D3 ... D3's instructions are explicitly retired by D31 and contradicted by D32', and the reader was right: it was handed two instructions that contradict each other. eb1c943e09b9's '[settled by D<n>]' annotation shows the answer beside the stale text and leaves the stale text in place. The fix was a hand fold through `artifact write` (F5, commons 35fa25a, /home/akien/.cairn/foreground-decisions.md line 345), which F5 names as follow-up (c): done by the door, not by hand.
traces_to: Law 4 (F5's 'done by the door, not by hand' becomes physics), Law 1 (a settled correction becomes structure instead of a hand rewrite re-derived each time), Law 5 (the file keeps the trail; the reader's view carries what is true now)
how: In cairn/machines/rehearsal/rehearsal.py add retire(ticket, ns, *, by, because, into=None, root=None). It reads the ticket and refuses, writing nothing and naming every lack in one Refused: an n in ns that is absent or already retired; a named entry whose 'by' differs from --by under cairn.tools.system_word.fold (his words move only by an answered question); a live (unretired, not in ns) line whose text, with any ' [settled by ...]' tail removed, matches r'\bD<n>\b' for an n in ns, naming that line's D<m> (a fold is finished, never left citing a retired line); an into that is absent, retired, or in ns; an empty because. On pass it stamps each named entry with retired = {by, at (UTC iso seconds), because, into (int or null)}, keeps 'text' untouched, and writes through _write_ticket (artifact door, verb cast) with why 'rehearsal: D<n>[,..] retired by <by>[ into D<m>]'. decision_ids_of excludes entries carrying 'retired'. reader_view drops retired entries from the pasted copy before labeling, and skips any '[settled by]' annotation whose settler or target is retired. In cairn/machines/rehearsal/__main__.py add `--retire D<n> [D<n> ...]` with `--because WHY` and `--into D<m>`. --by is required, as with --decide. --retire is mutually exclusive with --decide, --proved and --standing. It exits 0 on write and 2 on Refused, and the usage block gains its line. A fold is `--decide` of the one corrected line, then `--retire <old ids> --into <new id>`. The new proof cairn/machines/rehearsal/proofs/test_a_superseded_decision_is_retired.py builds fixture tickets in a tmp commons (root=), stubs no reader (it calls retire, reader_view and decision_ids_of directly), declares PROVES {'4968b5d18645': {'1':..,'2':..,'3':..,'4':..}}, and runs only through bin/cairn test. No existing proof is edited.
falsifier: RED if after the build: (1) on a fixture whose D3 is contradicted by D22, after decide() of a corrected D5 and retire([3, 22], by='cc', because=..., into=5), reader_view's pasted copy contains D3's or D22's text, or decision_ids_of still holds 3 or 22, or the file has lost either text, or either entry lacks retired.by/at/because/into; (2) retire of a line whose by is 'akien' with by='cc' does not refuse, or writes anything; (3) retire of D3 while a live D4 says 'per D3' does not refuse naming D4; (4) into an absent or retired id does not refuse. WRONG INTENT if over the next five tickets that need a correction CC still rewrites decision text through `artifact write` instead of the verb, or a retired line's text is lost from a ticket file.
